stories.title: Paired DNA strands recognize shape, not just sequence, in new small-molecule sensing method
stories.summary: You have probably performed a sandwich assay before, even if you didn't know it. Sandwich assays are the molecular sensing technology behind lateral flow tests like the at-home COVID test. After a sample is dripped onto the test strip, it combines with detector antibodies attached to tiny gold particles, which bind to any viral proteins present. When the sample reaches the test line, a second antibody anchored to the strip binds to a different site on the viral protein, creating a molecular "sandwich." As the gold particles accumulate, the test line turns dark red, becoming visible to the naked eye.

The Bank rate has fallen from its 2023-24 peak of 5.25%, although the Bank's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has left the rate unchanged at its last six meetings.

stories.title: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch may now have so much plastic, it’s changing the color of the ocean
stories.summary: The ocean’s blue and green hues near the infamous zone of debris have gotten brighter over the last 20 years, satellite data show The Great Pacific Garbage Patch , an area in the Pacific Ocean where debris naturally accumulates, is full of tiny bits of plastic. So full, in fact, that it seems to be changing the color of the ocean. The ocean is, of course, famously blue. That’s due to the wavelength of light it reflects . Water scatters shorter wavelengths, which we see as blue—while absorbing longer wavelengths such as red or orange. Additives in the ocean can affect its color, including phytoplankton, algae and sediment.
